name: paw-avatar
summary: A glass puppy head whose 15 agent states (idle, thinking, working, sleeping, error...) morph into each other, with a gaze that follows the pointer. The pose is a pure function of time, so it pauses, scrubs and exports frame-exact.

state.description: Which state to hold. One of idle, happy, excited, curious, thinking, working, focused, surprised, sleeping, wink, confused, sad, love, celebrating, listening.

speed.description: Time multiplier for the whole engine. Clamped to 0.1-10.

cycle.description: Seconds per state when walking every state in turn; 0 holds the chosen state.

track.description: Follow the mouse pointer with the gaze. Set data-fx-track="false" to hold the state's own gaze.

deviations.what: The character is ours. Upstream's PROFILES arrays and its 14 states are frame-by-frame measurements of the x.ai bot; none of those numbers are here. The Paw is drawn in art/paw-os-glass-puppy.svg, and this effect casts that drawing's three paths to radial profiles at load.
deviations.why: Upstream's own README says its MIT licence covers the code, not the visual design it recreates. Porting the engine and bringing our own drawing is the only use of it that is ours to ship.

deviations.what: The silhouettes come from an authored SVG parsed at load (flattenPath, ours) rather than from arrays traced off video frames, and the head and each ear are separate profiles instead of upstream's single blob.
deviations.why: Upstream traced a reference video and had no path to read; we have the drawing itself, so the drawing stays the source and the numbers are never hand-copied. Separate profiles let the ears pass behind the head and rotate about their own pivot, which a one-blob model cannot do.

deviations.what: Poses interpolate the ear rig (angle, lift) and each silhouette is placed from it per frame, instead of lerping two sampled radius arrays as upstream's blend() does.
deviations.why: A lerp between two outlines crossfades an ear; lerping the rig rotates it. Upstream has one body and no limbs, so the question never came up there.

deviations.what: Silhouettes are sampled at 96 angles, not upstream's 64.
deviations.why: The drawn ear is thinner than anything on a single blob and blobs out at 64 samples.

deviations.what: Rest gaze is square on (yaw 0) where upstream's is a measured 3/4 view (yaw 28.49, pitch 28.62, roll -13), and eyefit.ts is not ported. Look is ported without its `spin`.
deviations.why: The Paw looks at the reader, and its eyes sit at 0.41 head half-widths, well inside the outline, so the eye-to-edge correction eyefit exists for has nothing to correct. `spin` serves upstream's intro animation, which has no counterpart here.

deviations.what: TypeScript ported to plain ES modules; the Vue component, decor.ts, cycles.ts, expressions.ts, skins.ts and all of src/ui are not ported.
deviations.why: paw-fx effects are framework-free vanilla with a mount() contract, and the skin is CSS custom properties rather than a JS skin table.
